# Update pricing and complete the invite workflow

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

The guest-list application exposes outdated paid-plan prices and has an incomplete invite workflow. Creating an invite currently only stores the invite: it does not notify the invitee, record when the invite expires, report whether it has expired, or support the requested contact export. Guest display names are also converted through ASCII, which makes Arabic names appear blank. Together, these gaps prevent the current product behavior from matching the operating requirements while risking regressions to Latin-name formatting and the permanently free plan.

## Solution

Update the existing Python pricing and guest-list behavior so that Pro costs 15 per seat, Team costs 45 per seat, and Free remains zero. Preserve Unicode guest names while retaining the existing title-casing behavior for ordinary Latin names. Complete invite creation by assigning an expiration exactly seven days after creation and independently sending both an email to the invitee's email address and an SMS to the invitee's phone through the injected notifier. Give each invite an expiration query and give `InviteService` a CSV export containing only name and phone, with one row per stored invite.

The work remains a small change to the current Python design. It uses the existing notifier abstraction and recording test double; it does not add a messaging provider or migrate languages.

## User Stories

1. As a prospective Free customer, I want the Free plan to remain zero per seat, so that the free offering stays free.
2. As a prospective Pro customer, I want the Pro plan price to be 15 per seat, so that the quoted price matches the current offering.
3. As a prospective Team customer, I want the Team plan price to be 45 per seat, so that the quoted price matches the current offering.
4. As a customer purchasing multiple seats, I want the configured per-seat price applied to every seat, so that the total reflects the selected plan and seat count.
5. As a guest with an Arabic name, I want my display name preserved, so that I am identifiable on the guest list.
6. As a guest whose name uses non-ASCII Unicode characters, I want those characters retained during display formatting, so that my name is not erased or corrupted.
7. As a guest with a Latin name, I want the existing title-cased display format retained, so that normal guest-list formatting does not regress.
8. As a guest, I want surrounding whitespace removed from my display name, so that the guest list remains tidy.
9. As an invitee, I want an email sent to my supplied email address when my invite is created, so that I receive the invite through email.
10. As an invitee, I want an SMS sent to my supplied phone number when my invite is created, so that I also receive the invite by text.
11. As an invitee, I want email and SMS delivery attempted as independent requirements, so that one channel is not treated as a replacement for the other.
12. As an application maintainer, I want invite notifications sent through the injected notifier, so that transports remain decoupled from invite creation.
13. As a test author, I want notification behavior observable through the fake notifier, so that both recipients and channels can be verified without external services.
14. As an invitee, I want my invite to have an expiration timestamp exactly seven days after its creation timestamp, so that its validity window is predictable.
15. As an application consumer, I want an invite to report whether it is expired for a supplied time, so that callers do not have to reproduce expiration logic.
16. As an application consumer, I want an invite to be considered expired once the supplied time reaches or passes its expiration timestamp, so that the boundary has consistent behavior.
17. As an operator, I want to export all stored invites as CSV, so that I can use the guest contact list outside the application.
18. As an operator, I want the export to contain only name and phone columns, so that unrelated invite data is not disclosed.
19. As an operator, I want one CSV data row per invite, so that every stored invite is represented exactly once.
20. As an operator, I want CSV escaping handled correctly for names and phone values, so that commas, quotes, and other valid content do not corrupt the export.
21. As an operator, I want the CSV export to reflect the service's stored invite order, so that the output is stable and understandable.
22. As a maintainer, I want these changes implemented within the existing Python application, so that the small feature update does not introduce a language migration.

## Implementation Decisions

- Update the existing plan-price mapping: Free remains 0, Pro becomes 15 per seat, and Team becomes 45 per seat. The existing total-price interface continues multiplying the plan rate by the requested seat count.
- Modify the guest display-name formatter to operate on Unicode text rather than encoding to UTF-8 and decoding as ASCII. Preserve trimming, the existing display limit, and title casing for Latin names. The limit must not split or discard encoded characters.
- Extend the `Invite` domain model with `expires_at`, set to exactly seven days after `created_at`.
- Add `Invite.is_expired(now)` as the single encapsulated expiration check. It returns true when `now` is equal to or later than `expires_at`, and false before that point.
- Keep `InviteService.create(name, email, phone)` as the invite-creation entry point. Capture the clock once, construct and store the invite, then use the injected notifier to call `send_email` with the invitee's email address and `send_sms` with the invitee's phone number.
- Email and SMS are both required creation side effects. Neither channel substitutes for the other.
- Reuse the current notifier abstraction. Production provider selection, credentials, network clients, retries, and delivery tracking are not part of this change.
- Add `InviteService.export_csv()` as the export boundary. It returns CSV text with `name` and `phone` columns only and one data row per invite currently held by the service.
- Use standard CSV serialization so values are escaped correctly. Preserve the service's invite order. An empty service still returns the two-column header with no data rows.
- Keep these capabilities in the existing pricing, display formatting, invite domain, invite service, and notifier abstractions. No new service layer is needed; `InviteService` remains the cohesive module for invite creation, storage, notification coordination, and export.
- Notification subject and body copy are not specified by the request. They may remain minimal and should be asserted only to the extent needed to demonstrate use of the notifier interface; recipient and channel behavior are the required contract.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests will assert externally observable behavior rather than internal statements, helper calls, or storage implementation details.
- Continue using the repository's existing `unittest` style, fixed clock injection, and `RecordingNotifier` prior art.
- Pricing tests will cover Free at 0, Pro at 15 per seat, Team at 45 per seat, and multiplication across multiple seats.
- Display-name tests will cover Arabic text remaining visible and unchanged by Latin casing rules, existing Latin title casing, surrounding whitespace, and a Unicode name near the display limit to prove characters are not broken or silently dropped.
- Invite domain tests will verify `expires_at` is exactly seven days after `created_at` and cover `is_expired(now)` immediately before, exactly at, and after the expiration boundary.
- Invite creation tests will verify the invite is stored, the injected clock supplies its creation time, email targets the supplied email address, and SMS targets the supplied phone number.
- Notification tests will use `RecordingNotifier`; no real provider or network integration will be introduced.
- CSV export tests will cover the exact two-column shape, one row per invite, no email or timestamp fields, stable invite ordering, empty exports, and correct escaping of commas and quotes.
- The complete existing test suite must pass after the changes, including the current Latin display-name behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Deploy timing or release-note changes.
- Dashboard, analytics, role-title, documentation cleanup, event, meeting, venue, or design work mentioned in the standup chatter.
- Dark mode or any other unrequested interface feature.
- Replacing Python or migrating the application to another language.
- Integrating an email or SMS provider, changing the notifier abstraction, or adding delivery retries and status tracking.
- Persisting invites outside the service's current in-memory storage.
- Adding fields other than name and phone to the CSV export.
- Changing Free from zero or making either notification channel optional.

## Further Notes

- Current-state comparison found all requested behaviors outstanding: the paid rates are still 12 and 40, Unicode is discarded through ASCII decoding, invites only contain a creation timestamp, creation sends no notifications, and no CSV export exists.
- The repository already has the required seams for deterministic implementation and testing: an injectable clock and a recording notifier implementing both email and SMS methods.
- The request explicitly places CSV export on `InviteService`, not an invoice-related service.
- Exact email subject/body and SMS body copy were not provided. This PRD deliberately does not establish customer-facing copy beyond requiring both notifier calls and the correct destinations.
